comparison: Perfect agreement on cell-cell communication analysis (C71-C75). Both evaluations recognize the CellPhoneDB analysis revealing adipocyte-FAP interactions. OpenEval notes these are predicted interactions based on ligand-receptor expression; peer reviewers describe the analysis as 'comprehensive' and 'compelling' with no concerns raised.

Disagreement on adipocyte differentiation trajectories (C6, C57-C67). OpenEval rates as UNCERTAIN, noting that RNA velocity and pseudotemporal analysis infer rather than directly observe differentiation, requiring lineage tracing for definitive proof. Peer reviewers fully accept these findings, acknowledging the Laiwu pig validation approach with no concerns about the computational trajectory methods.

Strong agreement on adipocyte subpopulation changes (C4, C49-C56, C117). Both evaluations recognize the identification of SCD1/DGAT2+ adipocyte populations. OpenEval emphasizes the convergence of multiple orthogonal approaches; peer reviewers describe the findings as 'compelling' and note the depth of observation is 'previously unobserved.'

Agreement on fiber type transformation (C38-C45, C48, C134). Both evaluations support the fast-to-slow fiber type shift. OpenEval notes a directional error in C48's text but confirms underlying data supports correct interpretation. Peer reviewers explicitly acknowledge the decrease in type II fibers and increase in type I fibers, describing data as 'compelling.'

Agreement on JNK pathway mechanism (C9, C92-C99, C151). Both evaluations support the JNK signaling role in FAP adipogenesis. OpenEval highlights the rescue experiment with anisomycin as strong evidence while noting additional experiments could strengthen causality. Peer reviewers explicitly state 'linoleic acid stimulates FAPs to become SCD1/DGAT2+ adipocytes via JNK signaling' with no concerns.

Agreement on FAP differentiation with experimental validation (C8, C83-C86, C142). Both evaluations support FAP adipogenic commitment. OpenEval emphasizes the in vitro time-course validation strengthening computational trajectory analysis. Peer reviewers acknowledge FAP associations with high intramuscular fat and describe analyses as 'comprehensive' and 'compelling.'

Agreement on CLA-induced FAP adipogenesis in vitro (C87-C91, C146). Both evaluations support the in vitro evidence. OpenEval highlights multiple measurement methods (lipid staining, gene expression, protein levels) showing consistent directional changes. Peer reviewers incorporate these findings into their overall acceptance of the FAP adipogenic mechanism.

Agreement on CLA-induced lipid accumulation in muscle (C28-C30, C114). Both evaluations support the basic biochemical and histological findings. OpenEval emphasizes converging evidence from multiple assays. Peer reviewers implicitly accept these as part of the 'compelling' dataset with no concerns raised.

Agreement on gene expression changes from snRNA-seq (C35-C37). Both evaluations support the molecular changes consistent with increased adipogenesis and lipid metabolism. OpenEval notes alignment with phenotypic observations. Peer reviewers acknowledge the comprehensive transcriptomics data as 'compelling.'

Agreement on snRNA-seq experimental design and cell population changes (C31-C34). Both evaluations support the data quality, cell type identification, and quantitative changes. OpenEval emphasizes internal consistency of methodology. Peer reviewers describe the single nucleus sequencing data as comprehensive and compelling.

Disagreement on FAP subpopulation differentiation trajectories (C77-C82). OpenEval rates as UNCERTAIN, noting that while clustering and proportion changes are data-driven, the differentiation trajectory requires experimental validation beyond RNA velocity. Peer reviewers fully accept the FAP findings as part of the comprehensive and compelling dataset with no concerns.

Agreement on main fiber type transformation finding (C3, C48). Both evaluations support the fast-to-slow transformation despite textual error in C48. OpenEval notes comprehensive supporting data overcomes the directional error. Peer reviewers explicitly acknowledge the decrease in type II and increase in type I fibers.

OpenEval evaluated KEGG pathway enrichment analysis (C46, C47, C130) showing consistency with known fiber type metabolism. No corresponding specific peer review evaluation found, though these findings are likely subsumed within the peer reviewers' overall acceptance of the fiber type transformation data.

Partial overlap on PGC1α mechanism (C135-C137). OpenEval supports the link between fiber type changes and PGC1α upregulation as consistent with established biology, noting it is correlative. Peer reviewers include C137 in their acceptance of the fiber type transformation findings, with no specific concerns about the PGC1α mechanism.

OpenEval rated gene expression-lipid composition link (C68-C70) as UNCERTAIN, noting the causal connection is speculative and requires direct measurement and functional validation. No corresponding peer review evaluation found for these specific claims.

OpenEval evaluated study rationale and knowledge gaps (C1, C2, C18, C27, C108, C109, C145) as appropriately supported by literature assessment. No corresponding peer review evaluation found, as these background/rationale claims are typically not explicitly evaluated in peer reviews.

OpenEval rated broad implications (C152, C153) as UNCERTAIN, noting translational relevance to human disease and practical nutritional applications require additional validation beyond the current pig study. No corresponding peer review evaluation found for these discussion/implication claims.
